Linea Avey (formerly known by her birth name '<nowiki/>''Linda Avey''' )([[née]] Bahnson{{citation needed lead|date = February 2024}}) is an American biologist and entrepreneur. She is known for co-founding [[23andMe]], a consumer genetic data company.<ref>{{Cite magazine | last=Goetz|first=Thomas|date=2007-11-17| title=23AndMe Will Decode Your DNA for $1,000. Welcome to the Age of Genomics | magazine=Wired.com | url=https://www.wired.com/2007/11/ff-genomics/ | access-date=2019-05-22 | issn=1059-1028}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Harmon|first=Amy|date=2007-11-17 | title=My Genome, Myself: Seeking Clues in DNA | work=[[The New York Times]] | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/11/17/us/17dna.html | access-date=2019-05-22|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><!--<ref name="linkedin-lindaavey">{{Cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/lindaavey/#education-section|title=Linda Avey|website=Linkedin|access-date=May 5, 2018}}</ref>--><!--NO REF HERE ESTABLISHES AVEY IS BAHNSON.-->

== Early life ==
Avey was born Linda Bahnson in 1960, in [[South Dakota]], United States.{{cn|date = February 2024}}  She attended [[Augustana University]], where she received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in biology, in 1982.<ref name=":1"/>{{third party inline|date = February 2024}}<ref name="Augustana-alumni-award">{{cite web | author = Augie.edu Staff | date = 2010 | title = Viking Days: 2010 Alumni Achievement Award Winners Recognized | work = Augie.com | url=https://www.augie.edu/sites/default/files/shared/viking_days_2010.pdf | access-date=5 February 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210825030416/https://www.augie.edu/sites/default/files/shared/viking_days_2010.pdf |archive-date=25 August 2021}} For an Augie.edu page linking to the award page, and listing other alumni award recipients, see {{cite web | author = Augie.edu Staff | date = 2021 | title = Past Alumni Award Recipients | work = Augie.com | url = https://www.augie.edu/alumni-association/alumni-achievement-awards/past-alumni-award-recipients | access-date=5 February 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210825030354/https://www.augie.edu/alumni-association/alumni-achievement-awards/past-alumni-award-recipients |archive-date=25 August 2021}} Note, at this second citation, the subject's middle name is given as Bahnson.</ref><!--DOB, POB, DEGREE NOT IN AUGIE.EDU CITATION.-->

== Early career ==
{{refimprove section|date =February 2024}}
Avey began her scientific career in 1982 at [[University of California, Irvine]] as a staff research associate.{{cn|date = February 2024}}<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bahnson|first1=Linda S.|last2=Buckpitt|first2=Alan R.|date=1986|title=Naphthalene metabolism by human lung microsomal enzymes|url=https://ucdavis.pure.elsevier.com/en/publications/naphthalene-metabolism-by-human-lung-microsomal-enzymes|journal=Toxicology|volume=41|issue=3|pages=333–341|doi=10.1016/0300-483X(86)90186-1|issn=0300-483X|pmid=3775781}}{{primary source inline|date = February 2024}}</ref>{{primary source inline|date = February 2024}}<!--PRIMARY RESEARCH PUBLICATION DOES NOT ESTABLISH FACTUAL CONTENT OF THE SENTENCE, OR RELATE REPORT AUTHOR NAMES TO THE TITLE SUBJECT.--> It has been stated that in 1985, she moved into various sales and business development in the fields of biopharmaceutical and academic research.{{cn|date = February 2024}} As of 2024, a site to which Avey submits information was stating that she had "over 20 years of sales and business development experience in the biopharmaceutical industry in [[San Francisco]], [[Boston]], [[San Diego]], and [[Washington, D.C.]]"<ref name=":1">{{Cite web | author = Avey, Linda & BigThink.com Staff | date = 5 February 2024 | title = Co-Founder, 23andMe | work = BigThink.com | url = https://bigthink.com/people/co-founder_23andme/ | access-date=5 February 2024 | quote = <small>Linda Avey has over 20 years of sales and business development experience in the biopharmaceutical industry in San Francisco, Boston, San Diego, and Washington, D.C. Prior to starting 23andMe, she developed translational research collaborations with academic and pharmaceutical partners for Affymetrix and Perlegen Sciences. Linda also spent time at Spotfire helping scientists understand the power of data visualization and at Applied Biosystems during the early days of the human genome project. The advent of high density genome-wide scanning technologies brought huge potential for significant discoveries. However, the lack of sufficient funding to enable adequate studies prompted Linda to think of a new research model. These ideas led to the formation of 23andMe. Her primary interest is the acceleration of personalized medicine, using genetic profiles to target the right drug to the right person at the correct dose. Linda graduated from Augustana College with a B.A. in biology.</small>}}{{third party inline|date = February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Linda Avey Biography {{!}} Booking Info for Speaking Engagements |url=https://www.allamericanspeakers.com/celebritytalentbios/Linda+Avey/412727 |access-date=2024-02-10 |website=www.allamericanspeakers.com}}</ref><!--EARLIER FORBES CITATION MOVED TO FURTHER READING. DOES NOT SUPPORT PRECEDING SENTENCE AT ALL.--> She worked at Perlegen Sciences, where she was part of the company's alliance management team, working on research collaborations and grant submissions to the [[National Institutes of Health]].<ref name="Forbes2024">{{cite web |last=Wishart-Smith |first=Heather |title=23andHim: The Untold Story Of 23andMe's Third Co-Founder |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/heatherwishartsmith/2024/06/25/23andhim-the-untold-story-of-23andmes-third-co-founder/ |website=Forbes |date=June 25, 2024 |access-date=July 27, 2026}}</ref> While at Perlegen, she worked on a [[Parkinson's disease]] study funded by [[The Michael J. Fox Foundation]], through which she met [[Google]] co-founder [[Sergey Brin]], whose mother had the disease.<ref name="Forbes2024" /> By late 2005, she had left Perlegen for [[Affymetrix]].<ref name=":1"/><ref name="Forbes2024" />

She also held positions at Spotfire,<ref name=":1"/>{{third party inline|date = February 2024}}<!--<ref>{{cite web |title=Spotfire |url=https://www.tibco.com/products/tibco-spotfire |website=TIBCO Software Inc. |access-date=10 December 2021 |language=en}}</ref> IRRELEVANT GENERAL CITATION--> [[Chemdex.com|Chemdex]],{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} [[Applied Biosystems]],<ref name=":1"/>{{third party inline|date = February 2024}} PerSeptive Biosystems,{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}<!--<ref>{{cite web |title=PerSeptive Biosystems |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=32884 |website=Bloomberg.com |access-date=10 December 2021}}</ref> IRRELEVANT GENERAL CITATION--> Molecular Dynamics,{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} and ''Waters Corporation''.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}<!--<ref>{{cite web |title=Waters Corporation |url=https://www.waters.com/ |website=Waters.com |access-date=10 December 2021}}</ref> IRRELEVANT GENERAL CITATION-->

== 23andMe and later career ==
In March 2006 Avey, [[Anne Wojcicki]], and Paul Cusenza founded [[23andMe]],<ref>{{Cite web| author = CNBC.com Staff | date = 22 May 2018 | title = 2018 Disruptor 50 Full Coverage: 7. 23andMe | work = [[CNBC.com]] |  url=https://www.cnbc.com/2018/05/22/23andme-2018-disruptor-50.html|access-date=July 20, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | author = Bay Area News Group & Baron, Ethan | date = 29 December 2017 | title = Genomics Company 23andMe to Launch Weight-Loss Study Focused on Diet, Exercise and Genes | work=[[Santa Cruz Sentinel]] | url=http://www.santacruzsentinel.com/business/20171229/genomics-company-23andme-to-launch-weight-loss-study-focused-on-diet-exercise-and-genes | access-date= 5 February 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | date = 26 February 2018 | title = Media Center: About Us | work = 23andMe.com | url=https://mediacenter.23andme.com/company/about-us/ | access-date = 5 February 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180226180950/https://mediacenter.23andme.com/company/about-us/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=2018-02-26 }}</ref> "one of the first, and only,{{what|date = February 2024}} companies to offer genetic profiles directly to consumers, rather than through doctors or researchers".<!--HERPER FORBES AND CNBC CITATIONS MOVED, AS THEY DO NOT SUPPORT ACTUAL SENTENCE CONTENT. ONLY CITATION SUPPPORTING "first" CONTENT IS THE FOLLOWING.--><ref>{{Cite news| author = Ferris, Robert | date = May 5, 2016 | title = You Don't Have to be a Genius to Contribute to Science, Entrepreneur Says | work=[[CNBC.com]] | url=https://www.cnbc.com/2016/05/05/anne-wojcicki-you-dont-have-to-be-a-genius-to-make-valuable-contributions-to-science.html | access-date=5 February 2024}}</ref> Avey left the company in 2009 but remained as a board member until 2011.<ref>{{Cite news| author = Peterson, Becky | date = 6 September 2017 | title = 23andMe Gets $200 Million in Funding to Bring its Genetic Testing to the Masses | work= [[BusinessInsider.com]] | url=http://www.businessinsider.com/23andme-gets-200-million-in-funding-2017-9 |access-date=5 February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Edmonds |first=Lauren |title=A 23andMe cofounder says the company 'lost its way' under the last leaders |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/23andme-cofounder-linda-avey-company-lost-way-2025-3 |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US}}</ref><!--MOVED 23andme.com CITATION AS DID NOT SUPPORT DEPARTURE OF AVEY STATEMENT; MOVED UP TO WHERE IT WAS RELEVANT.--> <!--NODAL EXCHANGE BOARD OF DIRECTORS PAGE LINK REMOVED, BECAUSE IRRELEVANT TO DEPARTURE FACTS. MOVED TO EXTERNAL LINKS.-->

collec[t]... phenotypic information".<ref>{{Cite web| author = Davies, Kevin | date = November 24, 2009 | title = Linda Avey on an Alzheimer's Brainstorm | work = Bio-ITWorld.com | Development |language=en}}</ref> 

Avey is an advisor to Verily Life Sciences.<ref name=":0" /> In November of 2023, Avey joined the Board of Directors of the Human Immunome Project (HIP).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kane-Hartnett |first=Liza |date=2023-11-30 |title=23andMe Founder Linda Avey Joins the Human Immunome Project Board of Directors |url=https://www.humanimmunomeproject.org/news/23andme-founder-linda-avey-joins-the-human-immunome-project-board-of-directors/ |access-date=2024-02-15 |website=Human Immunome Project |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2026, Avery serves on the Board of Directors of Perlara, a biotech company seeking cures for rare diseases.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Perlara PBC: accelerate the discovery of cures across diseases |url=https://archive.perlara.com/about-us/ |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=Perlara |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[23andMe]] filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in March 2025 <ref>https://www.cnbc.com/2025/03/26/23andme-co-founder-lashes-out-at-ceo-wojcicki-after-bankruptcy-filing.html</ref>
